Elon Musk post on Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 hardware and planned additions: The reproduced post states Colossus 1 had 150,000 H100, 50,000 H200, and 30,000 GB200 processors, and Colossus 2 had 110,000 GB200 and 440,000 GB300. It says another 220,000 GB300 would be fully operational the following week, another 220,000 in November, and a further 220,000 by late December only “if we get lucky.” It does not mention Minihard or deployment costs. (time=2026-09-25T05:16:00Z; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
SpaceX EU Prospectus, June 5, 2026: The prospectus says Colossus II had brought online a second cluster of 110,000 GB300 processors and expected its next phase, once fully operational, to add at least 220,000 GB300 processors and over 400 megawatts of compute power. This is a prior company expectation, not confirmation that later capacity became operational. (time=2026-06-05; cutoff=BEFORE_CUTOFF).
Elon Musk Deploys 660,000 Nvidia GB300 GPUs for Colossus in Q4: The supplied item describes three 220,000-unit additions and also asserts a Minihard deployment and per-installment/total dollar values. Those facility and cost assertions are not present in the reproduced Musk post. The live page could not be verified as a pre-cutoff version. (time=UNKNOWN; cutoff=UNKNOWN).
